macro.regime: Equities bounce, AI credit stays distressed: a fragile risk-on with live two-sided catalysts
macro.narrative: Monday's US close confirmed a genuine, broad-based rebound from Friday's AI-credit scare -- S&P 500 +0.41% to 7690.73, Nasdaq +1.11% to 26430.89, and VIX collapsing 7.75% to 18.44 -- after Goldman Sachs upgraded CoreWeave to Buy and its 5Y CDS eased to roughly 1,082bp from Thursday's record ~1,194.5bp; but Oracle (~288-315bp) and SpaceX (~203bp) CDS spreads still pushed to fresh records on a reported $40bn SpaceX raise to buy Nvidia chips, so credit investors remain far less convinced than equity investors that AI-financing stress has passed. China's Q3 GDP beat at 4.5% y/y (vs 4.4% consensus, up from 4.3% in Q2), with September retail sales (+1.1% y/y) and industrial production (+5.5% y/y) both accelerating to their best pace since March, though export-driven strength masks weak domestic demand and a -20.6% YTD collapse in property investment; the PBOC's 09:00 SGT LPR decision today is expected to hold both the 1-year (3.00%) and 5-year (3.50%) rates for a 16th straight month. Oil fell further Monday (WTI -3.12% to $98.25) on Trump's Russia-sanctions waiver easing global fuel-supply fears even as Hormuz tanker attacks remain at wartime-record pace and Russia's Lavrov is in Tehran pressing de-escalation after Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait within seven days -- a live, two-sided catalyst, not a resolved one. The Fed remains in blackout ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC with hold odds near 84-87% (Kalshi/Polymarket/CME) and a still-hawkish ~14-15% hike probability priced (essentially zero for a cut), while this week's megacap earnings gauntlet (Netflix today, Tesla and Meta Wednesday) and Monday's French-protest-driven European equity selloff (Stoxx 600 -0.8%, CAC -1.6%, DAX -1.4%, FTSE -1.3%) add fresh, idiosyncratic swing factors layered on top of the AI-credit and Hormuz stories.
